title: L-1011 TriStar & Citation Sovereign+ In MSFS! | New Marketplace Aircraft
description:
Are you looking to expand your virtual hangar in Microsoft Flight Simulator this week, or are you trying to avoid impulse buys on the storefront? Today, we break down a diverse wave of brand-new aircraft arrivals on the MSFS 2020 Marketplace—spanning from iconic widebody trijet airliners and advanced corporate business jets down to rugged bush STOL turboprops and recreational ultralights.

To help you decide what fits your flight routine and budget, we inspect these new Marketplace releases and detail what each developer brings to the platform:

FSX 360 Lockheed L-1011 TriStar & Livery Pack: The legendary widebody trijet lands in MSFS 2020 with modeled flight engineer stations, custom C++ WASM system architecture, inertial navigation support, and over 1,900 interactive cockpit controls. We look over the freighter configuration, system coverage (hydraulics, bleeds, DLC, and autoland), and the dedicated 8K livery expansion pack covering British Airways, Delta, Eastern, Cathay Pacific, and LTU.

Skyward Simulations Cessna Citation Sovereign+: A high-fidelity modern business jet built for high-altitude climb and short-field versatility. We evaluate the custom Garmin G5000 implementation (custom PFD, MFD, and GTC touch controllers), dual FADEC systems, onboard EFB with SimBrief integration, passenger cabin detailing, and real-world pilot inputs.

Microsoft & AT Simulations Antonov An-28: Arriving in tandem with the latest World Update, this Ukrainian twin-turboprop STOL light utility aircraft offers rugged bush capability, dual-language cockpit labeling, and bundled passenger, cargo, and Antarctic explorer schemes—complete with MSFS edition upgrade discounts.

Italian Studio Works (ISW) Evektor EV-97 Ultralight: A crisp, recreational two-seat microlight featuring 4K PBR surface textures, realistic wear-and-tear cockpit modeling, steerable nosewheel dynamics, and dual-language documentation for relaxing low-and-slow VFR flying.

Whether you are plotting retro intercontinental schedules in a trijet or taking short-field executive hops, we evaluate this ramp inspection to help you decide what truly deserves a spot in your simulator installation.

If you enjoy honest, clear, and critical looks at the Flight Simulator Marketplace without the fluff, make sure to hit that like button, subscribe to the channel, and drop a comment below! Which aircraft are you adding to your hangar first?
